mainTopic: Who holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם; and whether one witness about a death is believed in cases of יבום
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of sages who hold that a person can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם, meaning something that does not yet exist or is not yet his. It first closes the story of רבי ינאי tithing fruit before it arrived. רבי ינאי dreamed of a 'bruised reed', and רבי חייא reassured him that the dream pointed to a comforting פסוק. Next the גמרא brings a source for each remaining name: רבי, from a ברייתא about a slave bought on condition to free him; רבי מאיר, from קידושין that take effect 'after' a later event; רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, from separating תרומה with fruit that is not yet ripe or picked; and רבי עקיבא, from a wife's קונם vow on work she has not yet done. Then a new topic begins: is one witness believed that a husband died, so that his widow may do יבום? רב ששת proves from a משנה about reversed testimony that one witness is believed. A second version says that question is obvious, since even the wife herself is believed. In that version the real question is whether one witness who says the יבם died frees the יבמה to marry anyone, and this question continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: So the tithing must have been on fruit that did not yet exist
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the story of רבי ינאי tithing fruit for שבת must be a case of a דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it a case like this one, where the fruit was not yet in the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its proof from the story of רבי ינאי: the only way to understand his tithing is that he tithed fruit that had not yet come into existence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other ways of explaining the story have been pushed aside, so the גמרא says 'it must be' the case of fruit not yet in the world. This shows that רבי ינאי held one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it…? (introduces the only remaining explanation)
Something that does not yet exist

phrases.english: Rather, is it not a case like this?
phrases.notes: He means the case of fruit that had not yet come into the world when it was tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof from the story of רבי ינאי, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ינאי holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי ינאי tithing fruit for שבת before it arrived

steps.title: רבי ינאי worries about his dream of a bruised reed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי tells רבי חייא he dreamed the words 'bruised reed' and fears it means he relied on something weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But in a dream they read to me 'bruised reed.' Weren't they telling me, 'Look, you are leaning on the staff of this bruised reed'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי asks רבי חייא whether his dream means he did something wrong by relying on this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'bruised reed' appear in a פסוק about trusting something weak that will break. רבי ינאי fears the dream is telling him that his act (tithing what did not yet exist) rested on a shaky basis.

keyTerms.meaning: They read to me in a dream
A staff, something you lean on

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי ינאי is speaking to רבי חייא.

phrases.english: But they read to me in a dream: "bruised reed";
Is it not that they were saying this to me:
"Behold, you have trusted upon the staff
of this bruised reed"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי ינאי, raising a doubt about whether his act was correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the dream mean that relying on a דבר שלא בא לעולם was a mistake?

steps.title: רבי חייא reassures him: it was a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that the dream referred to a different פסוק, a comforting one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, this is what they were telling you: 'A bruised reed he will not break, and a dim wick he will not put out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא tells רבי ינאי that the dream pointed to a different, positive פסוק, so he acted properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words 'bruised reed' also appear in a פסוק in ישעיהו that continues 'according to truth he will bring justice.' So the dream supports רבי ינאי's act, and both רבי חייא and רבי ינאי hold that a דבר שלא בא לעולם can be acted on.

keyTerms.meaning: He will not put it out

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows that both רבי ינאי and רבי חייא hold one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

phrases.english: No, this is what they were saying to you:
"A bruised reed he shall not break,
and a dimly burning wick he shall not quench."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ינאי's worry from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dream referred to the comforting פסוק in ישעיהו, so the act was correct.

steps.title: רבי's view: a slave bought on condition to free him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a ברייתא to show that רבי also holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי — as it was taught: 'Do not hand over a slave to his master.' רבי says: The פסוק is talking about someone who buys a slave on condition to free him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next name on its list, רבי, and brings a ברייתא as the source for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads the פסוק as talking about a buyer who bought a slave in order to free him. The buyer may not keep him as a slave, which implies the freeing worked even though it was arranged before the buyer owned him. The exact case is explained in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi — as it was taught:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, the next one on the list who holds this view.

phrases.english: "You shall not deliver a slave to his master";
Rabbi says: Regarding one who buys a slave
on condition to free him, the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רבי ינאי and starts proving the view of the next name, רבי.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the פסוק 'לא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו'

steps.title: What exactly is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the case of buying a slave to free him works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case behind רבי's words; this sets up the answer of רב נחמן בר יצחק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply promising to free a slave would not stop the buyer from keeping him. So we need a case where the slave is truly free, and that will show how it connects to a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? How does this case look?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case of רבי's ruling in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case of buying a slave on condition to free him

steps.title: He wrote: 'When I buy you, you own yourself from now'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the buyer wrote to the slave, before owning him, that he would belong to himself once bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He wrote to him, 'When I buy you, you are hereby owned by yourself from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the exact case: the buyer freed the slave in writing before he even owned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of writing, the slave did not yet belong to the buyer, so the buyer was giving away something not yet his. Since רבי says the slave goes free, רבי must hold that one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

keyTerms.meaning: You are owned by yourself (you are free)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי frees the slave even though the buyer freed him before owning him, so רבי holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Where he wrote to him: When I buy you,
you are hereby acquired by yourself from now.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דִּכְתַב לֵיהּ לִכְשֶׁאֶקָּחֲךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The buyer wrote, before owning the slave, that once bought the slave belongs to himself from now.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's view: קידושין that take effect 'after' a later event
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה where רבי מאיר says קידושין work even when the woman is not yet available to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר — as we learned: If a man tells a woman, 'You are married to me after I convert, after you convert, after I am freed, after you are freed, after your husband dies, after your sister dies, or after your יבם does חליצה with you,' she is not married. רבי מאיר says: she is married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to רבי מאיר and brings a משנה as the source for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case listed, the קידושין cannot work right now, so the man is acting on something not yet in existence. The חכמים say it does not work, but רבי מאיר says it does, which shows he holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds קידושין can work for a time when the woman is not yet available, so he holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם; the חכמים disagree.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir — as we learned:
One who says to a woman:
"You are hereby betrothed to me
after I convert," "after you convert,"
"after I am freed," "after you are freed,"
"after your husband dies," "after your sister dies,"
"after your yavam performs ḥalitza with you" —
she is not betrothed.
Rabbi Meir says: She is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי to the next name on the list, רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about קידושין that take effect 'after' a later event

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב also holds one can act on what is not yet in the world
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב lets a person set aside תרומה for fruit that is not yet ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, as a ברייתא teaches: Moreover, he said that even if someone says 'The picked fruit of this garden bed shall be תרומה for the fruit still growing in the bed,' or 'The growing fruit shall be תרומה for the picked fruit, once it reaches a third of its growth and is picked,' and it then reaches a third and is picked, his words take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another תנא to its list of those who hold that one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם. It brings a ברייתא about setting aside תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the man speaks, the growing fruit is not yet ripe or picked, so it cannot yet become תרומה or be obligated in it. Still, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says his words take effect once the fruit ripens and is picked. That means a statement can take hold on something that is not yet in a fitting state.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן
A third of the fruit's ripeness
His words stand and take effect

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov — as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Moreover, Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov said:
phrases.notes: "Moreover" points back to an earlier part of this ברייתא that the גמרא doesn't quote here.

phrases.english: even if he said
"The picked fruit of this garden bed

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּ תְּרוּמָה עַל פֵּירוֹת עֲרוּגָה מְחוּבָּרִים״,
phrases.english: shall be terumah for the still-attached fruit of the garden bed,"
or "the still-attached fruit of the garden bed
shall be terumah for the picked fruit of this one,
once they reach a third and are picked,"
and they did reach a third and were picked —
his words stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another תנא to the list started with רבי and רבי מאיר
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about תרומה from unripe, unpicked fruit

steps.title: רבי עקיבא also holds a vow can take hold on what is not yet in the world
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows רבי עקיבא worries that a wife's vow could take hold on work she has not yet done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא, as the משנה teaches: If a wife says 'Whatever I make for your mouth is forbidden like a קונם,' the husband does not need to cancel the vow. רבי עקיבא says he should cancel it, in case she makes more than she owes him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי עקיבא as the last name on its list. He holds that a vow can take hold on things that don't exist yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ת״ק says the husband need not cancel, since the vow is on work not yet done. רבי עקיבא says he should cancel it, because the vow could take hold on her extra future work. This shows he holds a vow can take effect on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a vow forbidding something
To cancel a vow, which a husband can do for his wife
She makes extra, more than required

steps.whatToRemember: The list of those who hold one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם: רבי ינאי and רבי חייא (from the dream story), רבי, רבי מאיר, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva — as we learned in a mishnah:
"Whatever I make for your mouth is konam" —
phrases.notes: The wife is vowing that the husband may not benefit from the work of her hands. That work hasn't been done yet.

phrases.english: he does not need to cancel the vow.
Rabbi Akiva says: he should cancel it,
in case she produces for him extra
beyond what is due to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final name in the same list of תנאים
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא holds a vow can take hold on a דבר שלא בא לעולם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about קונם שאני עושה לפיך

steps.title: Is one witness believed for a woman going to יבום?
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רב ששת whether one witness saying the husband died is enough to allow יבום. The two sides depend on why one witness is believed in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: what is the law for one witness in the case of a יבמה? Is one witness believed because a person won't lie about something that will come out, so here too he won't lie? Or is it because the woman herself checks carefully before she remarries? Here, since she may already like the brother-in-law, maybe she won't check carefully before marrying.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. The students ask whether we trust one witness who says a woman's husband died, so that she may marry his brother through יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one witness is enough to let a woman remarry, but the reason is unclear. If the reason is that a witness won't lie about something that can be found out, it works for יבום too. If the reason is that the woman checks carefully, it may not work here, because she may want the brother-in-law and not check.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died childless, waiting for יבום
Likely to come out and be discovered

phrases.english: They asked Rav Sheshet:
One witness in the case of a yevamah, what is the law?
phrases.notes: One witness says her husband died, so she would now go to his brother for יבום.

phrases.english: Is the reason we accept one witness because
a person does not lie about something that will be found out,
and here too he will not lie?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: טַעְמָא דְּעֵד אֶחָד מִשּׁוּם —
phrases.english: Or perhaps the reason for one witness is
that she herself checks carefully and only then marries.
And here, since sometimes she loves him —
phrases.notes: "Him" is the brother-in-law. She already knows him and may want to marry him.

phrases.english: she does not check carefully before marrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the דבר שלא בא לעולם list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one witness is believed about the husband's death to allow יבום, depending on the reason one witness is normally trusted

steps.title: רב ששת answers from a משנה about reversed testimony
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת cites a משנה where a woman did יבום based on testimony, and later the testimony was reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You already learned it. If they told her 'Your son died, and afterward your husband died,' and she did יבום, and later they told her the opposite, she must leave, and both the first and the last child are ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins answering by quoting a משנה. He will use it to figure out whether one witness is believed for a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son died first, the husband died childless and יבום is required. If the husband died first while the son was alive, there is no יבום and the brother-in-law is forbidden to her. The משנה says that when the second report reverses the first, she must leave, so רב ששת will now ask what kind of testimony this was.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it in a משנה
A child from a forbidden relationship

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it:
If they said to her: Your son died
and afterward your husband died, and she did yibum,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמְרוּ לָהּ חִילּוּף הַדְּבָרִים —
phrases.english: and afterward they told her the opposite —
phrases.notes: Now they say the husband died first, while the son was alive. So there was never any יבום.

phrases.english: she must leave,
and the first child and the last child are mamzerim.
phrases.notes: Children from the brother-in-law, whether born before the second report or after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question by citing a משנה
steps.raayaObject: The law of one witness for a יבמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of מת בנך ואחר כך מת בעליך

steps.title: The משנה cannot be talking about two witnesses against two
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules out reading the משנה as two witnesses against two, since then there is no reason to follow the second pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it was two witnesses against two, why rely on these second witnesses? Rely on the first ones!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts narrowing down what case the משנה means. He rules out the case of two witnesses against two. This sets up the next move, where he will show it must involve one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses against two are equally strong, so the second pair should not be able to force her out. Since the משנה says she must leave, it cannot be talking about two against two. The גמרא is building toward a case that answers the question about one witness.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
What did you see to prefer one side?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If we say it was two witnesses against two —
what did you see that you rely on these,
phrases.notes: "These" means the second pair, the ones who reversed the story.

phrases.english: rely on these instead!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה just cited by testing which case it must be
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the משנה as two witnesses against two
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Two against two are equal, so the second pair could not force her to leave

steps.title: A second reason the משנה cannot be two witnesses against two
steps.stepSummary: If two witnesses contradicted two, the child would only be a doubtful ממזר. Yet the משנה calls him a definite ממזר, and it is clearly speaking precisely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, why call the child a ממזר? At most he is a doubtful ממזר! You might say the תנא was not being exact. But the last part of the משנה says 'the first is a ממזר and the last is not a ממזר.' That shows the משנה is choosing its words exactly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a second argument against reading the משנה as two witnesses against two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two pairs of witnesses contradict each other, we don't know who is right. So a child from that marriage could only be a doubtful ממזר. The משנה calls him a full ממזר, and its careful contrast in the סיפא shows it means this exactly. So the two-against-two reading falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: a person who may or may not be a ממזר
was not being exact in his wording
the last part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: And furthermore, a ממזר?
He is only a doubtful ממזר!
And if you say the תנא was not exact,
but from the fact that the last part teaches:
The first is a ממזר
and the last is not a ממזר,
learn from it that it teaches precisely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection of the two-against-two reading from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the משנה as two witnesses against two.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would make the child only a doubtful ממזר, but the משנה precisely calls him a definite ממזר.

steps.title: So one witness is believed for יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must be about one witness who was contradicted by two. That shows that one witness, if no one contradicts him, is believed to allow יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we must learn from it that it was one witness. The only reason his word is set aside is that two came and contradicted him. Otherwise, he would be believed.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the other reading failed, the גמרא concludes the משנה is about one witness. That answers the question from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses beat one, which is why the first testimony is overturned. But the משנה lets the woman do יבום on the first witness's word. So with no contradiction, one witness is believed to allow יבום.
steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, one witness is believed to say the husband died, even to allow יבום.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not to be learned from it: one witness.
And the reason is that two came and contradicted him,
but if not so, he is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the alternative reading rejected, completes רב ששת's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One witness is believed to say the husband died, even to allow יבום.

steps.title: A second version: the first question is not a question at all
steps.stepSummary: Another version says no one would ask whether one witness allows יבום. A משנה teaches that even the wife herself is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: you shouldn't ask this, because even she herself is believed. We learned in a משנה: a woman who said 'my husband died' may remarry. If she said 'my husband died,' she may do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the question. It first says the original question was too obvious to ask. This sets up a new question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wife's own word is enough to allow יבום, a witness is surely believed too. So step 10's question has an obvious answer. The real doubt must be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: you should not ask this; it is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against רב ששת's proof. It is a different version of what the students actually asked him.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
This you should not ask,
for even she herself is also believed,
as we learned in a משנה:
A woman who said "My husband died" may remarry.
"My husband died": she may do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר: הָא לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of the question from step 10 and says that question is obvious.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the wife alone is believed to say her husband died, both to remarry and to do יבום.

steps.title: The real question: can one witness free a יבמה to marry anyone?
steps.stepSummary: In this version the question is whether one witness who says the יבם died lets the יבמה marry anyone. It depends on why one witness is believed: either he won't tell a lie that will come out, or the woman checks carefully before marrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where you should ask is about freeing a יבמה to marry anyone. Why is one witness believed? If it is because a person won't lie about something that will come to light, then here too he won't lie. Or perhaps one witness is believed because she checks carefully before she marries. But this woman doesn't check carefully, because the יבם is hated by her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the real question in this version and lays out its two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one is that the witness won't lie when the truth will come out. That applies here too, so he would be believed. Reason two is that the wife checks before remarrying. A יבמה who dislikes the יבם is glad to be free of him, so she won't check, and the witness might not be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow waiting for יבום with her late husband's brother
a matter that will eventually come to light
she checks carefully and only then marries

steps.whyThisMatters: The two reasons for believing one witness about a death lead to different results. Here they decide whether a יבמה can go free.
